question: An engineer must configure SAN connectivity in Cisco UCS Manager. The requirement is to specify the WWPN of the storage array and set the zoning type to Single Initiator Multiple Targets. The engineer must also configure interrupt handing and queues of the vHBA interface. Which two Cisco UCS polices should be used to configure the settings? (Choose two.)
theory: SAN connectivity design in Cisco UCS Manager splits responsibilities between two policy types: a storage connection policy defines the storage array's WWPN targets and the desired zoning topology (such as Single Initiator Multiple Targets), controlling how the vHBA's traffic reaches specific storage targets, while a Fibre Channel adapter policy tunes lower-level vHBA driver behavior such as interrupt handling and queue depth/count for performance. Boot policy, a generic 'vHBA policy' (not a real UCS object), and SAN connectivity policy (which bundles storage connection policies for use in a profile, rather than defining WWPN/zoning itself) don't match both requirements the way these two policies do. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Storage Management, Storage Connection and FC Adapter Policies)
